Automated Brinell Testing Principles
The operational theory behind our Automated Inline Hardness Tester relies on the traditional Brinell method, but we have completely modernized the execution. The system determines material toughness through a highly specific, carefully controlled mechanical squeeze, seamlessly processing parts like train wheels ranging from 700 millimeters to 1300 millimeters in diameter without missing a beat.
Here is how the automated methodology actually handles the physical testing:
Integrated Surface Preparation: Before any pressing happens, the machine physically mills or grinds the exact testing spot. This ensures a perfectly clean surface, wiping out any interfering mill scale or rough rust.
The Heavy-Duty Motorized Actuator: This setup replaces manual hand-cranks with a smooth, electric-powered drive that applies the exact Brinell testing force required, holding the pressure perfectly steady.
Smart-Eye Cameras and Image Processing: Instead of relying on manual calculations, an ultra-sharp optical system captures a high-resolution snapshot of the squished-in mark to determine the diameter.
Closed-Loop Force Control and Inline Integration
If you have ever watched two different operators try to read the same manual test dial, you know how incredibly frustrating it is when they argue over the final numbers. That is why our Automated Inline Hardness Tester series (which includes the Bre-Aut MAR for raw parts, the Bre-Aut SOR for finished components, and the Bre-Aut SOR with Fixed Clamps) runs on a smart, closed-loop feedback loop.
The electronic controller communicates directly with the motor, ramping up the pressing force as smooth as silk. This guarantees zero jerky movements and incredibly consistent load application. Heavy-duty structural frames block out harsh factory floor vibrations, ensuring the mechanical application never loses its settings and every single testing cycle goes off flawlessly.
Optical Evaluation and Verification Logic
Normally, a technician has to squint through a microscope lens to measure the tiny borders of a test mark, which can be a slow, eye-straining process. Our automated method completely replaces that subjective guesswork. Using high-resolution lenses paired with intelligent image processing, the system identifies the exact edges of the indentation, even if the metal surface is slightly scruffy or unevenly finished. You get laboratory-grade precision in the blink of an eye, and the resulting data is sheer perfection.
Furthermore, the testing protocol features a brilliantly strict verification method. If a component falls outside the required specifications, the system automatically shifts over and runs two additional measurements exactly 25 millimeters away to double-check the results. It then applies a highly visible paint mark on the non-conforming items and exports all the measurement data instantly, keeping your production line moving with absolute ease.
